attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: A present-tense statement about commitments already made. The firm floor is 20%. The 30-40% range is correctly kept as a hedge and isn't scored.

contract.note: Measuring against contracted backlog is an ordinary reading of 'commitments... of cloud revenues in the coming years.' It cuts both ways: uncontracted future revenue would lower the share, but Microsoft's RPO includes non-cloud software. The contract also checks against a reasonable revenue estimate.

evidence.note: Combined backlog of about $2.33T for the four sellers as of mid-2026, drawn from their filings. This is the denominator.
OpenAI's commitments total about $688B across three sellers, Google excluded. That is about 29.5% of e1's total, above 20%. Secondary source, available before the evaluation date.
Derived from Microsoft's own disclosure: OpenAI is at least about 32% of Microsoft's June 2026 backlog.
Recognized revenue (7% of Microsoft's total) is a different metric. The same source puts OpenAI at about half of Oracle's backlog.

reviews.rationale: OpenAI's commitments to Microsoft, Amazon and Oracle (about $688B, Google not counted) come to about 29.5% of the four sellers' combined mid-2026 backlog. Microsoft alone is about 32-41% and Oracle about half, both well above the 20% floor. Measured against all future revenue the share would be lower, but the gap from 20% is large and Google's commitment is left out of the numerator, so the firm claim holds.

attribution.note: Zitron's own accusation against Nadella in his own post.

semantics.note: A factual charge that Nadella deceived investors. The proposition matches the statement.

contract.note: 'Misled' is a charge of deception, so asking for an identifiable misleading statement or a finding is fair. The speaker gave no period and didn't say whether he meant false statements or selective framing; the contract flags both.

evidence.note: The class action is pending and Microsoft denies it. As reported, it concerns Azure growth and AI spending, not revenue concentration. No finding.
Implies OpenAI is a large share of Nadella's $37B AI run rate. That is an implied ratio and doesn't show a specific statement was false.
The CFO gave backlog growth excluding OpenAI. That partial disclosure cuts against a charge of concealment.
Microsoft disclosed OpenAI's roughly 45% share of its backlog. Backlog is not AI revenue, but it weakens the concealment charge.

reviews.rationale: No court, regulator, or company finding shows that Nadella misled investors about AI revenue concentration. The only lawsuit is pending and is about other issues. The packet identifies no specific Nadella statement shown to be false. Microsoft did disclose OpenAI's share of its backlog and growth excluding OpenAI, which cuts against the claim but doesn't refute it. The evidence doesn't settle it.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: Present-tense claims about Anthropic's losses and commitments. 'Can't keep' is an undated judgment about the future that can't be tested yet, as the contract notes.

contract.note: Reading 'unprofitable' as operating loss is ordinary. Cash flow points the same way. GAAP net loss would favor the speaker, but most of Anthropic's net loss is a non-cash charge from its rising valuation, and the contract reports it as context.

evidence.note: Per the S-1 as reported: Anthropic's H1 2026 operating loss was $0.69B, operating cash flow was positive, and Q2 showed an operating profit.
Per the WSJ: OpenAI's H1 2026 operating loss was about $21.6B, roughly 30 times Anthropic's.
Anthropic has $518B in future infrastructure commitments, which matches 'hundreds of billions'.
Anthropic's $80.7B net loss is about 90% non-cash fair-value charges. It doesn't show comparable operating losses.

reviews.rationale: The commitments part holds: Anthropic has committed $518B in future infrastructure spending. The core comparison fails: Anthropic's H1 2026 operating loss was about $0.69B against OpenAI's roughly $21.6B, and its operating cash flow was positive. Anthropic's large net loss is mostly non-cash fair-value charges. Whether it can keep its commitments can't be tested yet.
